messages:
maria: Heads-up — PM/console asked for a per-1k-token unit-economics view that breaks down cache and batching savings. Need infra + runtime signals to compute this end-to-end. Who owns the data plumbing?

ben: I can help. Which exact metrics do you need from the runtime vs infra?

maria: Minimal set: total_tokens, cached_tokens, batched_tokens (or batch_size histogram), model_variant, request_count, gpu_seconds, and egress_bytes. Plus cost tags: instance_type, region, and billing_rate at hour granularity.

devon: runtime can emit total_tokens and KV cache hits (so cached_tokens = cache_hits * avg_cached_prefix_tokens). Batch sizes we have as distribution per node but not aggregated per route. We'll need a rollup job.

leah: infra side: we can provide gpu_seconds and billing_rate from infra billing export (bigquery). Egress_bytes is available. Mapping request -> instance_type needs the routing_id tag to be passed through logs.

maria: ok. Two integration concerns: 1) attribution: attribute tokens to customer route/model_variant. 2) aggregation window: console wants daily and 1h rollups.

ben: Attribution: runtime already attaches model_variant and route_id to traces. We need to ensure those fields are present on the metrics stream (not just traces). Currently metrics are per-host.

devon: Quick note: emitting per-request token counts on the hot path adds overhead. We can emit token deltas at completion as a lightweight counter and attach labels route_id/model_variant. That should be cheap.

leah: For batch savings we need to know baseline per-token latency to estimate how many tokens would have been sent without batching? Or do we show actual measured cost reduction from batching/cache using two numbers: raw_tokens vs charged_tokens?

maria: Prefer measured: show gross_tokens (what user sent), served_tokens (what runtime produced), cached_tokens, and effective_charged_tokens = served_tokens - cached_tokens_adjusted - batching_savings. We need a clear definition for "batching_savings" — proposal: compute difference between sum(individual_token_cost_estimate) and actual cost after batching using per-node observed GPU_seconds allocation.

ben: That gets messy quickly. Alternative: expose two dashboards — 1) raw telemetry (tokens, cache_hits, batch_hist), 2) cost model that joins telemetry with infra billing to compute cost_per_1k = (gpu_cost + egress_cost + infra_overhead) / (charged_tokens/1000). Keep cost model offline (daily job).

devon: I agree. We'll emit the low-latency telemetry metrics to metrics-prod with labels: route_id, model_variant, region, batch_size_bucket. Then an hourly ETL job can join with billing to produce per-route per-model cost.

leah: We'll need stable keys. route_id has multiple formats (legacy vs new). I'll push a compatibility layer so ETL can map both. Also suggest adding a "deployment_phase" tag (canary/steady) for rollouts cost comparisons.

maria: Nice. Console UX asks for a single view: cost_per_1k, cache_percent, batching_effectiveness, and a table of top routes by monthly spend. Also want anomaly alerts when cost_per_1k increases >10% wk-over-wk for a route.

ben: For alerting, we should compute relative week-over-week in the ETL and emit metric cost_per_1k_change_pct. That avoids doing joins in alerting infra.

devon: Implementation tasks from runtime: 1) emit counter token_total {labels}, 2) emit counter cache_hits {labels}, 3) emit histogram batch_size {labels}. Will add an opt-in flag per deployment.

leah: Infra tasks: 1) publish hourly billing export to bq table with instance_type/cost per hour, 2) supply mapping table for route_id->customer_id, 3) provide egress price config.

maria: Data engineering/console: 1) define ETL transform to compute charged_tokens and cost_per_1k, 2) define dashboard panels and alert rules, 3) retention policy and sample queries for debug.

ben: Dependencies: runtime changes (devon) + infra billing mapping (leah) + ETL job (data-eng). ETA? devon can do runtime changes in 2 sprints if we keep fields minimal.

devon: 2 sprints fine. Will open PR with metrics schema and example prometheus exposition.

leah: Infra mapping & billing export: I can prioritize this week; expect table live in BQ in ~5 business days.

maria: I'll create the console spec doc and example visual mockups. Can we sync on Thurs 10am to align on schema?

ben: works for me. :thumbsup:

devon: I'll drop the metrics schema in the PR and tag you, @maria.

telemetry-bot: Reminder: please include metric names in snake_case. Example suggestions: tokens_total, cache_hits_total, batch_size_histogram, gpu_seconds_total.

maria: Thanks — will use those names in the spec. Action items summarized:
- devon: PR with metrics emission (tokens_total, cache_hits_total, batch_size_histogram) and opt-in flag.
- leah: BQ billing export + route_id mapping table.
- ben: ETL template + join logic for cost_per_1k.
- maria: console spec + mockups + Thurs 10am sync.

leah: One more: what about cardinality? route_id+model_variant+region can explode. Suggest limiting model_variant to canonical names and bucketing batch_size to <4, 4-8, 8-16, 16+.

devon: Agreed. We'll canonicalize model names and emit batch_size_bucket label.

maria: Great. I'll create the follow-up thread with links to the PR, BQ table, and draft dashboard after the sync. Thanks all. :rocket:
